title: Request Sleuth — Failure Triage Dashboard & Payload Investigator
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a first-class failure triage surface in the Redwood Console called 'Request Sleuth'. The goal is to help engineers and SREs quickly understand why requests fail, whether retries are effective, and what payload/state contributed to the error. Key capabilities: (1) concise failure summary with derived error taxonomy and confidence score, (2) request timeline with retry waterfall and latency breakdown, (3) payload snapshot and diff across retries (headers, prompt, model args, cached KV), (4) grouped examples for the same error class with sampling, (5) quick actions: re-run (sandboxed), create support ticket (with context), pin/ignore error class, and export payload for security review. Non-goals for this ticket: implementing backend sampling APIs (ENG), full audit-log playback (separate initiative). Personas: platform engineers onboarding incident response, ML engineers debugging quality regressions, PMs reviewing customer-impacting errors. The design should prioritize readability at small card sizes for high-density dashboards and progressive disclosure for payloads (collapse long inputs, redact sensitive fields by default).
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype covers summary card, timeline/waterfall, payload snapshot, and grouped-examples panel
Design spec includes interaction details for re-run sandbox, export flow, and redaction toggle
Figma prototype shared with engineering and PM with explicit API contract stub in Confluence
Accessibility: keyboard navigation for timeline and payload inspection, color-contrast passes AA
Performance note: prototype shows lazy-loading strategy for payloads to reduce rendering cost
comments: 2025-02-10 — Aisha Raman: Kickoff notes. Initial sketches attached in Figma (link below). Primary ask came from two customer incidents where retries masked the root cause; customers want to know 'why a retry succeeded' vs 'why it failed' in first place.

2025-02-11 — Tomás Ortega (Eng): Backend requirements: we need request-level snapshots from the sampling pipeline (ENG-4921). We'll also need a new endpoint for diffing stored payloads; engineering can provide a draft API by 2025-02-20.

2025-02-12 — Evelyn Park (Design): Iteration 1 prototype pushed to Figma. New structure: top summary ribbon, middle timeline with retry lanes, bottom accordion for payload/diff and grouped examples. Sharing with PM for prioritization.

2025-02-13 — Maya Chen (PM): PM feedback: add a 'customer-facing explanation' generator for support bundles that summarizes root cause in plain language. Also prioritize export-to-ticket flow for enterprise customers.

2025-02-14 — Accessibility review (internal): Suggestion to make retry waterfall keyboard-focusable and provide aria-live updates when payload loads. Also call out redaction defaults for PII — require security review.

2025-02-15 — Eng design review (Tomás Ortega): Concern noted about rendering huge payloads in the browser for large prompts. Proposal: stream a compact preview and lazily fetch full payload on demand; also limit number of grouped examples to 10 by default.

2025-02-16 — Evelyn Park: Updated prototype link and interaction notes uploaded. Added microcopy for 'redact sensitive fields' toggle and 'explain this error' button (invokes backend explainability job). Preparing handoff doc for 2025-02-18 design review.

2025-02-17 — Aisha Raman: Design decisions captured: (1) error taxonomy will be shown as badges with primary/secondary tags and confidence, (2) timeline will visualize token-level delays when available, (3) quick actions will be contextual and gated by RBAC. Next: finalize specs and mark ready for engineering grooming.
